questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I knew the language (English)
Wasn't too far from home
Beautiful nature
Well acknowledged univeristy

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not particularly easy. I would say that my host institution was better at providing information than my home institution. Information came little by little which makes sense in not making the information load too big all at once but sometimes that also left you quite in the dark if the information that you needed didn't come yet

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A online group meeting with a person who helped international students during their stay

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I got a twin room very very last minute because I called

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Breakfast and dinner was served. A pantry was available but with only a toaster and a kettle

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It can be very intense to eat you meals with hundreds of other students but it is also a good possibility to get to know other people

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to fill out some stuff online which was a little confusing because you didn't really get any confirmation and then had to show up with your boarding pass and passport which went pretty smoothly considering how many students had to go through that process

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I wrote an e-mail to ask if I filled out the forms online correctly

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got one out of three classes that I initially applied for

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If in doubt, send an e-mail

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took nursing courses and sociology courses in order to be able to get some credits transferred even though I study psychology so I think it was hard to know anything about the level

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It seemed a bit more fragmented. The texts that we read wasn't part of the lectures in the same ways (only some lecturers included the readings). Also the seminars and the lectures didn't really related which can be a strength in terms of covering more topics but a weakness if you wanted to get a better understanding of the lecture or readings

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Psychology of Conversation
Designing and doing social research
Mental health: Life sciences and nursing care 2

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Psychology of conversation was a really nice elective course because I felt like I learned a lot. Mental health: Life sciences and nursing care 2 was also a really nice course but not particularly suited for psychology students

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I joined the hill walking club and we were on some amazing trips

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of activities and clubs were available. The non-academic opportunities is what makes University of Edinburgh really great in my opinion

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined the hill walking club and we were on some amazing trips

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go hiking!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. I think Scotland and Denmark are pretty similar. Of course it was different but not in a degree so that it was hard to adapt

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a club or a society and show up to their socials

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: People screaming at each other on the streets. People showing of their anger in public generally. I don't feel like that really happens in Copenhagen.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People were generally very open

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. There is a lot of administrative work that has to be done which can be very time consuming and frustrating but it is all worth it. 
2. Call the people with student accommodation. We were a lot of students who got student accommodation last minute because we called. 
3. For me school was second compared to getting new experiences and meeting new people and I'm very happy I prioritized it like that

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Amazing experiences in nature and meeting some very nice people

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not having any time alone - I lived in a twin room and also had a very social life

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
